  Hiking routes here take approximately 1 to 3 hours.

Two viewpoints overlook the village of Ahuano, the Napo River and its smaller tributaries. During the walk, your guide points out local plants and explains how they are used.

After the hike, you can float downstream along the Arajuno River on inflatable tubes. The Amazoonico rescue center is located on the same river. It cares for injured and confiscated wild animals and, whenever possible, returns them to their natural habitat. A visit offers a chance to see local wildlife that is difficult to spot on an ordinary jungle walk.

The return boat ride to Casa del Suizo takes around 15 minutes.

You will also learn about the blowgun once used by jungle communities for hunting. Visitors who wish to can try aiming at a target.

On the way back, stop at a pottery workshop. A craftswoman demonstrates how traditional pieces are made by hand using natural materials from the Oriente region. The group then visits a woodcarving workshop to watch bird figurines being created.

The trails vary in length and difficulty, with walks taking between 1 and 4 hours. The route crosses streams and hills before reaching a viewpoint. A local guide explains how the Kichwa people use rainforest plants in daily life and traditional medicine.

After the hike, you can float downstream on a balsa-wood raft. The journey lasts around 30 minutes and ends near Casa del Suizo.
